title: Best visual tracker
body: This isn’t just about habits. It’s really great for tracking anything you want to log on a daily basis. I’ve been through a few of these apps and this is the only one worth paying for. The simplicity is really perfect here. Log the habit and see a nice monthly or yearly view of how often or when you did it. You can spot patterns you didn’t realize existed. It also helps as a motivational tool. You don’t have to remember to do whatever it is you’re trying to do, you just have to remember to open the app. Seeing the days blank motivates you to get a thing done. I’m guessing the dev is a fan of the GitHub commit tracker because that’s basically what I was looking for except for logging things like “practice guitar” or “exercise” or whatever. It’s good for quitting smoking as well. So many uses and you only pay once which is refreshing in the current year.

title: Satisfyingly checking off habits
body:

Forget cutesy interfaces, overuse of emojis, and overwhelming looking reports with annoying fonts. No one needs all that.

This app has a clean interface, visually appealing monthly and yearly report, and each check-off of a habit is so so satisfying. I paid for the full version to create more habits, but even so - it’s lifetime access, instead of a subscription which was what I was looking for, plus you’d be supporting small developers. Thank you for creating this app! I look forward to using it for many years to come!

title: (Updated) Great app!
body:
Really like this app, but it desperately needs an easier way to edit habits for past dates. Presently, if I want to add 3 tasks I completed yesterday, that requires 15 taps! WAY too cumbersome. The best option would be to simply allow users to tap on the date for the applicable habit under the “(Current Month)” page. The fact that this page doesn’t have that functionality is baffling. Alternatively, a swipe gesture could be added to the “Today” page. Where swiping right takes you to an identical page for Yesterday, then the previous date. Even if users could only go back in time 2-3 days using this method, that would be enough. With one of these features, this is definitely a 5-star app!

(Updated to 4 stars - thank you devs for the response!  Turns out there’s a super helpful shortcut via long-pressing the habit on the home page to mark yesterday as complete. That solves 90% of the struggle here!  5 stars once the calendar updates are complete.  Really glad I’ve found a habit tracker I can stick with!)

title: Super Habit = Atomic Habits!
body:
I love Super Habit, it is the perfect digital companion to the book Atomic Habits. After reading the book I struggled to find the perfect app to track my newly forming habits. Using a paper tracker was a PITA for my digital nomad life. Which brings me Super Habit. 

What a game changer! One of the biggest challenges of maintaining habits for me, was living on the road. Every new destination was new chaos for my life and trying to get into my daily routine usually failed. 

But with Super Habit I start my day, no matter my location, with my “list” of habits and voilà — much less chaos. Seeing my past success helps keep me motivated. 

There's only one tiny, insignificant detail I wish it had, which is why I rated it 4 ⭐️ instead of 5. 

If you could mark the habit done from the notifications screen, instead of taking you INTO the app, it would be perfect! I have other tracking apps that let you do that, but they lack all the great features of Super Habit. 

Also, the customer service and support are awesome 👏🏻 

Thanks!

A lot of the habits that I set up would be easier to measure by allowing me to enter a target quantity for a specific daily, weekly or monthly habit and then entering the quantity accomplished as I go. For example, if my habit is to run X number of miles per week. I’d like to keep tally of the miles as I run them. title: This app is CHANGING MY LIFE ! ! !
body:
Habit Tracker—or Super Habits as it was called when I downloaded it on my phone—now I purchased Premium version for my iPad as well!  
This is the app I USE MOST of all my apps, EVERY SINGLE DAY.  It is the appI use ALL THROUGHOUT my day, and it is MY MOST IMPORTANT APP for my life satisfaction.  It is my most important app because I love opening it and using it every day, throughout the day.  
I follow my Habit Tracker first thing in the morning (phone on Do not disturb so I’m not interrupted by calls/notifications), I have an AMAZING day. At the close of the day I have done the things that are most important to me to do.  Before Habit Tracker use, I had a very hard time focusing on and DOING, the things that are important to me.
I used this to track when I got off sugar in April and I now have 26 days off sugar and sweeteners, I have SO MUCH MORE ENERGY AND PEACE OF MIND.  I am enjoying being alive SO MUCH.
  I love being able to change the colors and make each habit a beautiful color that is a “Ching!”—Reward—to see when I check it for the current day! And seeing the colors together as I progress down my habit list makes me very happy. Kevin has created two of my most used apps. He really works on them and utilizes feedback and makes them the best—and the ideas for the apps are just so USEFUL and pertinent to enriching lives! They are the best apps I have. (The other app I use a lot is MEMY—to memorize and/or read over one or two of my most important sayings, quotes, pieces of poems or of what I am learning.)

title: Cool app
body: Easy to use, simple layout, v cool to watch your goal numbers go up.  If you forget to check in for a day or a few days you can easily go back and check off for the day(s) you missed.  Thanks for a great app, Kevin😊
author: sskicks

title: Great App for Habit Tracking
body: Love the app. Easy to use, keeps me on track and focused on a goal and helps me stay accountable!
author: Genzie66

title: Great app
body: Simple, to the point, and without unnecessary features.
author: Chief Magoo

title: I love this app!
body: As I evaluated my daily habits earlier this year, I realized that part of the reason I don’t accomplish more of my goals is because I get distracted and lose track of the daily tasks that are required to successfully complete my larger goals. I use this app everyday to remind myself of those smaller tasks. I look at it very quickly when I wake up and this helps me to push back distractions like checking email or social media until I have done the tasks I created in the app. I rarely pick up my phone and mindlessly look through it because I can easily use this app to remember tasks on my phone that make good use of my time such as listening to a new podcast or sending a note of encouragement to someone I know. The app is easy to use and worth the price in my opinion.
author: Familyeight

title: Exactly what I was looking for
body: I like the minimalism of this app. It has been instrumental in starting and maintaining consistent habits. I’m able to easily see my progress and have visual incentive to perform my habits to keep my streaks alive. By the way, I purchased the app. I am normally content with the free version of an app but it was well worth it for extra features.

author: daveblueheron

title: Beautiful, clear tracking
body: Frictionless, beautiful tracking of your daily, weekly, monthly habits. I use it everyday and am glad I found it. I use the free version and it is great. Highly recommend.
author: Uqushbrja737

title: Awesome way to quickly track stuff
body:
Been using this app for a while, and it’s a great way to quickly check off that you’ve done those routine things you do. 

For me, I’ve got it set for workouts, taking vitamins, stretching, and work reminders too. I love being able to look at the history and go, “oops definitely slacked last week” and it helps keep you accountable by being able to see how you’re progressing through a week when checking things off.
author: Scanner guy

title: Perfect for Seinfeld writing strategy
body: This app is perfect for Jerry Seinfeld’s method of forcing himself to write. I use it to write at least something every day - no zero days- and it works! I refuse to break the streak - holidays, vacations, traveling, whatever!

The dev is passionate and is very responsive to feedback. The application is constantly approving. If you’re thinking about it go for it! Take it from a penny pincher.

body:
Beware, this is a useless app!

author: Peyotlz

title: My preferred habit tracker!
body:
The UI is so simple, clean, and easy to understand! It is not time consuming to use. After setting up the desired habits and finish them with a tap. I love how I can input my old data into the app. 

The free trial version only allows two habits to be tracked. The one time fee for unlimited trackable habits is so worth it because of the other useful features (dark mode, importing data, reminders, even changing the app color!)   

I love that there are no subscription fees and my data isn’t stored on a server! I don’t rate and buy  apps usually. Buying this app definitely was worth helping out a solo developer!
author: uyui03

title: Love Habit Tracking!
body:
I love the idea of habit tracking — from exercising (and having separate habits for each excerise I want to do) to eating healthy or going without spending. I’ve tried bullet journaling but it was hard to stay accountable for that, as I much prefer this digital means. On the free version, you can track two habits. I upgraded for $9 so I could get unlimited habits and dark mode (love that feature as well!) The upgrade to premium mode helps support an independent developer as well, so if you really like the app and can spend the money, I would recommend updating to get the unlimited habits and to help support the developer. 

The app interface is clean and easy to navigate. You can make this app work for whatever your needs are! Plus, the reminders are fantastic, as you can set up a certain amount of them per week (3 per week, every day, etc.) I find that extremely helpful to keep track of remembering to log your habits. A+!
author: nicomulder

title: Very good set of features, no subscription
body:
I’ve downloaded like, 20 different ‘habit’ apps and this one has many of the features and design I look for: 
- easy to tally habit as done, and they’re all on one page
- shows week,month, and year overview progress
- no subscription model for premium
- can tally previous days if you forget
- individual reminders and can have multiple of them
- shows streaks 

I’d like some badges/achievements, the ability to track negative habits (eg smoking), and also the ability to track multiple reps per day (eg if you want to keep track of glasses of water you’re drinking or pull-ups etc).
author: logmasterd

title: Love this app
body: This is the best App I’ve been able to find to keep me on track. It helps me keep focused on my daily exercise, my eating habits, like NOT eating things that I love that are bad for me and how many days I can go without eating CANDY. I’m a diabetic and it’s real challenge for me. There are so many things in my life that I  do that I want to stop doing and things that I don’t do that I want to start doing and I keep track of with this app. Needless to say I really like the app and I use it every single day to log my results with just a tap. I’ve been trying for 20 years to lose weight and this app has given me the extra help that I have needed to accomplish my weight loss goal. I finally got under 200 pounds by setting a goal not to eat after 6 PM, not to eat candy and things like that. The simple process of setting a goal and checking off every day showing that you’ve done what you planned really helps. I know that there are other good apps out there to accomplish the same thing but this one really works for me. I like simple, straightforward, uncomplicated easy to use apps that accomplishes my desired results. Oh, I don’t usually do reviews but I like this app so much that I went on and on and on. Sorry! Give it a try, I think you’ll like it!
author: Rednoc

title: Lost all data
body: For seemingly no reason, all my data was erased from this app. I lost months of habit tracking and there doesn’t seem to be a way to restore it.
author: Roberstar

title: Gold star habit tracker 🌟
body: Simple and clear interface, wonderfully user friendly. I use this app every single day - what a gem!
author: Another flipping nickname

title: Just what I was looking for!
body: I have tried many habit apps but this design and interface is by far the best and most motivating
author: GamerGlitches

title: Thoughtfully designed, useful app
body:
I have been using this app daily since 9/27 to track both good and bad habits. It's well designed, useful, and my favorite app in the quantified self category. I would only ask for two changes. 

1. The app is designed around positive habits that you want to sustain (e.g. exercise). It does not cater to habits you want to quit. It's subtle, but things like "TO DO," streaks, and minimum goal of 1/wk instead of 0. It's not hard to work around that, but for example I'd rather not see "TO DO" next to bad habits. Just an empty state check box is enough for both good and bad habits. 

2. It would be cool to stack different habits on one graph for comparison. But again, it's not hard to work around by just exporting the data.

body: Not interested in a simple app that won’t log even 1 week of data. I’m profienct and couldn’t get it to work even for this. Plus multiple pop up screens. No thanks, Kevin
author: AnnieOakley*****

title: Exactly what I was looking for
body: Simple yet effective! It’s easy to use and gives me a little box to tick and something to show for my efforts. I being able to see my progress
author: Bski6

title: Wonderful app and responsive creator
body:
I love this app for tracking daily habits. I haven’t tried weekly or x-times per week habits yet, but I expect to try that soon.
Pros- 
-Really easy to check off the box for previous days (useful for when I complete tasks after midnight but before bed, or when I work night shift so my days are not 12am-12am)
-great improvement to show the calendar week instead of the last 7 days! I track things by calendar week
-intuitive and satisfying to use
-the “zoomed out” view of 2019 of the past year is super motivating as the months go by
-nice to have % success rate because that’s how I evaluate myself
Cons-
-it would be nice to have a chance to look at a month zoomed out, and see % success rate for each month. I’m hopeful that the creator will continue to add features though, he has done so since I found the app from a reddit thread 6 months ago or so.
I’m a happy premium member!
author: I Use It Daily!

title: Thoroughly impressed.
body:
I was having a rough night. This lifted my spirits. Played with with some, then purchased it. Was this created by one day as well? You! Should be very proud of yourself. And you inspire me to do more and help me see the true potential of humans. 
The app has features that aren’t in other apps similar to this. Which makes it unique. AND it’s not complex at all, it’s almost too simple. But it’s the perfect amount of functionality for now. And with the help of people like me (I’ll at least try) we can help this developer with such an amazing app.

title: One simple tweak to be best habit tracker I’ve used
body: The simple visual layout of each habit and the streak is perfect. I just wish you were able to designate a time frame for a specific habit. For example 4 days a week of exercise per week. Seems like it’s just for habits you want to do daily.

body: Really like the app so far, it’s minimalistic and non intrusive. I would like if habits could be categorized by good or bad.
author: Balbo_Baggins

title: Close to greatness
body:
From a UX standpoint, this is one of my favorite habit tracking apps. The haptic feedback adds a layer of tactility, and the dark UI is nice and clean. 

As of right now, it’s lacking a few key things that I personally need in a habit tracker. Mainly, the need for streaks to be set up with number per week, or specific day setup. Adding negative streaks would be a nice addition as well. 

I’m excited to see where this app can go from here, and I don’t think it’ll be long before it’ll be a staple for me.

author: dylanelson

title: Great app, bad execution
body:
This is a great. However limiting the test user to 2 habits and asking for $5 is a horrible decision. It only gets this app deleted after a one star review. 

Here is a tip: do what you’re doing on the app it’s great. Give the user 21 days of all bells and whistles (to form a habit). Once you hook them on, charge them whatever fee you want. Although I believe it should be $2.99. You should make money from quantity. Since it’s easier to pay $2.99 vs $5.99.
